chunks: Do not disregard the rights of your brother, relying on what is between you and him,
for he is not your brother if you disregard his rights.
And let not your household be the most miserable of people through you,
and do not lean towards him who turns away from you,
and let not your brother be stronger in disregarding kinship with you than you are in maintaining it with him,
and do not be stronger in responding to evil than you are in doing good.
and do not feel too much the oppression of a person who oppresses you, for he is only busy in harming himself and benefiting you,
The reward of him who pleases you is not that you displease him.
ai.seo_question: How should one respond to the oppression of others according to Imam Ali's instructions to Hasan?
ai.summary: Delivered as parting counsel to his son Hasan after the Battle of Siffin, this passage underscores the strategic importance of preserving familial and social bonds amidst political turmoil. Imam Ali (peace be upon him) warns against letting minor grievances sever kinship ties, emphasizing that true brotherhood is defined by the fulfillment of rights rather than mere proximity. He further instructs Hasan to respond to oppression with magnanimity rather than reciprocal harm, ensuring that his household remains his source of peace rather than misery.
